name: Gamaliel (Pharisee, teacher of Paul)
title: The Wise Teacher of the Law
summary: Gamaliel was a highly respected Pharisee and teacher of the law in Jerusalem, known as Gamaliel the Elder. He was the grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel and the teacher of Saul (the apostle Paul). He is best known for his wise counsel to the Sanhedrin to let the apostles go free, arguing that if their work was from men it would come to nothing, but if it was from God, no one could stop it.

keyEvents.title: Advice Regarding the Apostles
keyEvents.description: When the Sanhedrin wanted to kill the apostles, Gamaliel stood up and gave wise counsel to let them go. He argued that if their work was from men, it would come to nothing on its own, but if it was from God, they could not stop it.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Teacher
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul states that he was brought up in Jerusalem and trained at the feet of Gamaliel in the law of our fathers, and was zealous for God.

keyEvents.title: Examples from History
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel used historical examples about Theudas and Judas the Galilean to show that false movements had come to nothing on their own, as an argument for leaving the apostles alone.
